trickyParts: up.test.sh sources up.sh minus its last line, so every top-level readonly runs at source time before the test exports SMOKE_PROJECT; the container name therefore cannot be a top-level readonly. It is derived in main() and passed to ensure_nats as $1 (a `readonly` inside main would also break the test, which calls main() four times).

up.test.sh stubs ensure_nats in its main() cases, so the record file is written by main() itself (beside webhook-mode), not by ensure_nats -- that is what lets the test assert the record without docker.
down.sh keeps the record after teardown on purpose: deleting it would make the next down.sh fall back to legion-smoke-nats, a container that may belong to an older rig still running.
